How to use Serumpun

From opening the page to comparing three-season rotation strategies. One screen at a time, with a picture of exactly what you will see.

Free, foreverNo account No ads or trackingWorks offline English + Bahasa Indonesia
Open the live app ↗

Use the ← → arrow keys, the buttons below, or swipe on a touch screen.

Step 1 of 11

Open the website

Open the address on any phone or computer. There is nothing to install and nothing to sign up for.

  • Tap Find my field to start with a real place.
  • Tap Use a sample field (offline) for a complete demo with no internet at all.
  • The ID / EN button in the header switches between Bahasa Indonesia and English.
  • Add it to your home screen from your browser menu — it keeps working offline afterwards.

Good to know · Everything here is free: no account, no ads, no tracking, no payment tier.

Step 2 of 11

Tell it where your field is

There are four ways to set a location — use whichever works on your phone.

  • Search a village or town name, then pick a result and confirm with Use this location.
  • Use my location asks your phone for GPS.
  • Drop a pin on the map, or type latitude and longitude by hand.
  • Use a sample field loads bundled Central Java data with zero network.

Good to know · No signal, or just looking around? The sample field still produces the full recommendation, rotation and strategy comparison.

Step 3 of 11

Check the field snapshot

Before recommending anything, Serumpun shows what the data says about the area around your field.

  • The KPI strip shows temperature, rain this month, soil wetness and elevation, each with its source.
  • Charts show the long-term monthly climate and the next 16 days of forecast.
  • A map shows the field with OpenStreetMap tiles and an optional NASA true-colour satellite layer.
  • Use What if I plant in a different month? to re-score for another planting month.

Good to know · These are regional estimates from grids and models, not measurements taken at your field.

Step 4 of 11

Describe your field · soil

Three short steps about your own plot. Step 1 asks about the soil.

  • Choose Sandy, Loam, Clay or Peaty — a one-line hint explains each.
  • Add a soil pH between 4.0 and 9.0 if you know it; leave it blank otherwise.
  • I don't know is always an acceptable answer.
  • If a soil service pre-fills a value, it is clearly labelled estimated — please check it.

Good to know · Your answers are labelled self-reported. Nothing is silently presented as a measurement.

Step 5 of 11

Describe your field · water & terrain

Step 2 captures the conditions that change how much water a crop really needs.

  • Can you water the field? — none, partial or reliable irrigation.
  • Is the field sloped? — flat, gentle or steep, which affects erosion risk.
  • How much shade the plot gets.
  • What surrounds it — forest, water, buildings or nothing in particular.

Good to know · These feed the water-fit, terrain/erosion and surroundings factors in the score.

Step 6 of 11

Describe your field · history & size

Step 3 is about what happened on this plot before, which drives the rotation advice.

  • What grew here last season? — pick a crop, or Nothing / unknown.
  • Set your priorities and an optional field size in hectares.
  • If the previous crop is unknown, the app assumes a neutral starting crop and says so.
  • Finish with See recommended crops.

Good to know · Nothing here is mandatory. The app degrades honestly instead of blocking you.

Step 7 of 11

Read your crop recommendations

Serumpun ranks 3–5 crops for this place and this month, with a score you can interrogate.

  • Each card shows a 0–100 score, a verdict, a planting-window chip and a confidence level.
  • Tap a card to see why it scored that way.
  • Use the month chips at the top to ask “what if I plant later?”
  • Open Scoring method to see all seven factor weights, or Download field card to keep a copy.

Good to know · Confidence is separate from the score. Low confidence means the data is thin — not that the crop is bad.

Step 8 of 11

Understand why a crop scored that way

Every point of the score is broken down into named, weighted factors.

  • Seven factors: temperature, water, soil, season, terrain, surroundings and rotation continuity.
  • Each factor carries its source, freshness and an estimated flag.
  • You also get things to watch, water need, typical days to harvest, difficulty and the planting window.
  • Continue with See 3-season rotation plan.

Good to know · Every number on this screen traces back to a named, keyless data source.

Step 9 of 11

Plan the next three seasons

One recommendation is only the start. Serumpun builds a sequence that keeps the soil healthy.

  • Season 1 is what to plant now; Seasons 2 and 3 are what to plant next.
  • The sequence avoids the same plant family, sequences nitrogen roles, alternates root depth and breaks disease cycles.
  • Why this change explains every transition, with a climate-fit note for that month.
  • Continue to Compare rotation strategies.

Good to know · Seasons 2 and 3 are tentative — check real conditions again before planting.

Step 10 of 11

Compare at least three strategies

Instead of one answer, you get several comparable options — including the rotation you already use.

  • The table compares soil health, water demand, nitrogen balance, bare-field weeks and rule violations.
  • Your current rotation is always included as a baseline, not as a recommendation.
  • Each strategy lists supporting evidence, benefits, information gaps and risks needing local review.
  • Open View this 3-season plan to inspect the sequence behind a row.

Good to know · On a phone, scroll the comparison table sideways to see every column.

Step 11 of 11

Check where every number came from

The last screen is the audit trail for the whole app.

  • A table lists every allowlisted host with its licence, status, freshness and contribution.
  • The scoring method and the crop database are documented in plain language.
  • Datasets that need an account or key are credited as inspiration only — they are never called.
  • Refresh data retries the sources; Start over clears the session.

Good to know · Only eight keyless hosts can ever be contacted. No API keys, no accounts, no telemetry.

You are ready
